questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 35-year-old woman was brought to the casualty ward with a history of road traffic accident (RTA) and head trauma. Her eye opens to pain, moans, can localize limb towards the pain stimulus on the left hand and away from the pain stimulus on the right hand and both the legs in extended posture. Calculate her GCS.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 9

The GCS (Glasgow Coma Scale) of this patient is E2V2M5, which comes to a total score of 9.
E2-Eye opens to pain
V2-Moans
M5-Localizes to pain on the left hand (the score represents the best performance elicited, which would be localizing towards the pain stimulus)

Revised Glasgow coma scale for head injury:

Minimum GCS is 3, maximum GCS is 15.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 40 year old female with burns over her abdomen, both limbs and back and presented after 8 hours. Which of the following is the formula for calculation of fluid infusion?
options: 2 ml/kg X %TBSA for the next 16 hours
5 ml/kg X %TSBA for the next 16 hours
4 ml/kg X %TSBA for first 8 hours then 2 ml/kg X %TBSA for next 16 hours
4 ml/kg X%TSBA for the next 16 hours
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 2 ml/kg X %TBSA for the next 16 hours

Fluid resuscitation in burns:

According to ATLS 10th edition, 2018, the resuscitation formula used in thermal burns is 2 mL/kg × % TBSA.

First 8 hours: 1 mL/kg × % TBSA (lactated Ringer solution)
Next 16 hours: 1 mL/kg × % TBSA (lactated Ringer solution)

For a patient presenting 8 hours after sustaining thermal burns, the total volume using resuscitation formula should be given in the next 16 hours i.e; 2 mL/kg × % TBSA in the next 16 hours while maintaining target urine output of 0.5 mL/kg/hr for adults.

In adults, urine output should be maintained between 30 and 50 cc/hr to minimize potential over-resuscitation.

Note:

The goal of resuscitation is to maintain the fine balance of adequate perfusion as indicated by urine output. It is important to understand that formulas provide a starting target rate; subsequently, the amount of fluids provided should be adjusted based on a urine output target of 0.5 mL/kg/hr for adults and 1 mL/kg/hr for children weighing less than 30 kg.

Total percentage of the burnt area is calculated clinically using the rule of nines.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A patient who was on ventilator and being ventilated for past few days suddenly pulls out of the endotracheal tube. What is the next step of management?
options: Watch for spontaneous breaths and reintubate if needed
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Watch for spontaneous breaths and reintubate if needed

About half of self-extubated patients may not require re-intubation. Pre-extubation FiO2, PaO2/FiO2, and ventilator mode, as well as gender, may be useful in determining the likelihood that a self-extubated patient will require re-intubation and also watch for spontaneous breathing.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Nerve fibre least susceptible to local anesthetic is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. C

The nerve fibre least susceptible to local anaesthetic is type C. The order of susceptibility of nerve fibres to local anaesthetics is B >A-δ > A-γ > A-β > A-α > C i.e

• B fibres are the most susceptible/least resistant
• C fibres are the least susceptible/most resistant

Factors that increase the sensitivity of nerve fibres are :

• Smaller diameter
• Unmyelinated nerves
• Anatomical and physiological factors

*Note: Although theoretically, C fibres are supposed to be the most susceptible to local anaesthetics, practically it was found to be the least susceptible.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: The time required for preoxygenation before tracheal intubation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 3 min

Preoxygenation with tidal volume breathing of 3 mins is required before tracheal intubation.

Preoxygenation or denitrogenation is the process of replacing nitrogen in the lungs with oxygen.

This delays the onset of critical hypoxia during the period of apnea by 5-8 minutes.

This lengthened apnea time provides an improved margin of safety while the anesthesiologist secures the airway and resumes ventilation.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which of the following can be used as an intravenous induction agent?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Lorazepam

Lorazepam is a benzodiazepine that can be used for induction of anesthesia at a dose of 0.1mg/kg, although midazolam is preferred among benzodiazepines.

Benzodiazepines are mainly used for sedation and less commonly for induction of anesthesia due to the availability of better induction agents (propofol, etomidate, ketamine, and thiopentone).

Dexmedetomidine is a selective alpha-2 agonist and is used primarily as an adjuvant. So, a better option would be lorazepam.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct sequence?
options: Assess the patient’s response, Activate ERS, check carotid pulse, Start CPR
Check carotid pulse, Start CPR, Call for help and activate ERS, Defibrillate
Defibrillate, Assess response, Check carotid pulse, Maintain airway
Start CPR, Activate ERS, Defibrillate, Check pulse
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Assess the patient’s response, Activate ERS, check carotid pulse, Start CPR

BLS sequence:

First step – Assess safety of the surroundings.

Second step - Assess for responsiveness

Third step – Proceed if the patient is unresponsive. Shout for help.

If the patient is unresponsive assess for breathing and carotid pulse simultaneously for no more than 10 seconds.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A patient is undergoing modified radical neck dissection (MRND) for laryngeal malignancy. While ligating the internal jugular vein, his etCO2 dropped from 40 mmHg to 14 mmHg, and the patient developed hypotension along with cardiac arrhythmia. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Venous air embolism

A drastic fall in etCO2 with hypotension during neck surgery is most likely due to venous air embolism (VAE).

In modified radical neck dissection (MRND), a head-up position is given to provide a bloodless surgical field. VAE into severed vessels is likely to occur when the surgical site is above the right atrium and venous pressure at the incision site is below the atmospheric pressure. Pulmonary artery pressure will rise and etCO2 will fall after a venous air embolism.

In sympathetic overactivity and carotid body stimulation, blood pressure will rise.

In vagal stimulation, a drastic drop in etCO2 is unlikely.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: At what level does the spinal cord end in adults?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. L1-L2

The distal termination of the spinal cord is the lower border of L1 in adults.

Because the spinal cord ends at L1, lower nerve roots course some distance before exiting the intervertebral foramina. These lower spinal nerves form the cauda equina.

Note:

In children, the spinal cord ends at L3 and moves up with age.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which of the following is not a contraindication to the use of morphine?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Acute myocardial infarction

Acute myocardial infarction is not a contraindication for morphine use.

Morphine is the opioid of choice for myocardial infarction as it relieves anxiety, chest pain, and myocardial oxygen demand.

Contraindications to the use of Morphine:

• Bronchial asthma: Histamine release can cause bronchoconstriction and precipitate attacks of asthma.
• Renal failure: Morphine-6-glucuronide (metabolite) can accumulate and lead to prolonged respiratory depression.
• Emphysema: Respiratory depression and decreased response to hypoxia can cause hypercapnia in patients with COPD
• Head injury: Hypercapnia due to respiratory depression can increase ICP. Miosis, vomiting, and effect on wakefulness make interpreting the signs of head injury difficult.
• Biliary colic: Constriction of sphincter of Oddi can worsen biliary spasm
• Hypotension and shock

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Duration of action of Proparacaine:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 20 min

The duration of action of proparacaine is approximately 10-20 minutes.

Proparacaine hydrochloride ophthalmic solution is used as a topical anesthetic agent.

Indications: For procedures which require corneal anesthesia of short duration such as:

• Tonometry
• Gonioscopy
• Removal of corneal foreign bodies
• For short corneal and conjunctival procedures

Contraindication: Patients with known hypersensitivity

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Glycopyrrolate is used as a pre-anesthetic agent for:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Reducing the secretions

Glycopyrrolate is used as a pre-anesthetic agent for reducing the secretions.

Anticholinergic drugs e.g. atropine, glycopyrrolate are routinely administered with anticholinesterases in order to attenuate the undesirable muscarinic effects. Glycopyrrolate is usually preferred because it has less vagolytic effects than atropine at doses that inhibit secretions and does not cross the blood-brain barrier. It should be administered as early as possible to maximize its effectiveness.

Glycopyrrolate 0.2 mg IV, is administered to dry airway secretions before flexible scope intubation of the trachea, during the bronchoscopic examination.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Identify the device shown in the image below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Automated External Defibrillator

The device is an Automated External Defibrillator (AED).

This is a special medical device that is commonly used for recognizing the absence/presence of rapid ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation. With no need for intervention by an operator, it determines whether an electrical shock right to the heart must be performed (defibrillation).

An automated external defibrillator can be used on those victims, who are unconscious and aren’t breathing in a normal way. As a rule, it is used together with CPR in cases of sudden cardiac arrest. It is forbidden to use it on patients who are less than eight years old or those weighing less than 25 kgs.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which is not an obvious advantage of high pressure oxygen through nasal cannula:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Decreases need of intubation

High flow nasal cannula (HFNC), which delivers oxygen at high flow, and pressure through the nasal cannula.

Advantages of high-flow nasal cannula:

• Soft and pliable nasal prongs provide comfort to the patient.
• Warming and humidification of secretions: The heating of air to core temperature and humidification of the inspired air is better at high-flow. The humidification causes increased water content in the secretions, which facilitates the removal of secretions. It also decreases the work of breathing and avoids airway dessication and epithelial injury.
• Reduces dead space: The high flow of the oxygen delivered clears the upper airway of the expired air, which reduces dead space by a decrease of rebreathing and allows a higher fraction of minute ventilation to participate in alveolar gas exchange.
• Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP): HFNC increases the positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), and reduces the work of breathing.
• High flow rate causes decreased entrainment of room air, allowing more accurate delivery of oxygen.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which of the following is not a risk factor for postoperative pulmonary complications?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Well controlled asthma

Well-controlled asthma is not a risk factor for postoperative pulmonary complications.

Risk factors for postoperative pulmonary complications:

1. Age >70 years
2. COPD (uncontrolled)
3. Neck, upper abdominal, Aortic, neurologic surgical procedures
4. Prolonged procedure >2 hours
5. General anesthesia with intubation
6. BMI > 30
7. Albumin concentration < 35 g/L
8. Inability to walk two blocks on level land or one flight of stairs

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: You are an intern posted in the ICU. While taking a blood sample for ABG, which of the following steps would you not do?
options: Normal ph can't rule out acid base disorder
Add 0.5 ml Heparin to the syringe before taking blood
If modified Allens test is negative, alternate site is chosen
Radial artery is the preferred site
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Add 0.5 ml Heparin to the syringe before taking blood

0.5 ml of Heparin is not added to the syringe before taking blood.

Very little heparin is needed in the sample to prevent clotting; 0.05 to 0.10 ml of a dilute solution will help prevent coagulation of 1 ml of blood without affecting its pH. This is achieved by drawing 0.5 ml into the syringe and flushing it out. The residue that remains adherent to the syringe is sufficient for the procedure.

Heparin must be added to the syringe as an anticoagulant. Because the pH of heparin is near 7.0, and the Po2 and Pco2 of the heparin solution are near room air values, excess heparin can alter ABG measurements. After flushing the syringe with heparin, a sufficient amount usually remains in the dead space of the syringe and needle for anticoagulation without distortion of the ABG determination.

Note:

• Modified Allen's test positive indicates that the collateral blood flow is normal
• Modified Allen's test negative indicates that the collateral blood flow is abnormal and an alternate site must be chosen.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A patient of blunt chest trauma has been started on mechanical ventilation. Which of the following is not correct about the initial setting?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Tidal volume - 12ml/kg of actual BW

The tidal volume of 12ml/kg of actual body weight is an incorrect initial setting for mechanical ventilation.

Initial ventilatory settings are as given below:

• Tidal volume - 4-6 ml/kg of IBW (Ideal Body Weight)
• Respiratory rate - 12 Breaths/ min
• FiO2 - 100% to begin with and titrated to lesser values to prevent oxygen toxicity
• PEEP - Begin with 5 cm H2O, titrate to 10 cm H2O (Carefully increased as high PEEP may impair ventricular filling in a patient with blunt chest trauma)

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Identify the equipment shown in the image below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. High flow nasal cannula

The equipment shown in the image is high flow nasal cannula.

High flow nasal cannula is a mode of respiratory support used in the management of acute respiratory failure. It delivers humidified gas via the nasal cannula at high flow rates.

• HFNC can deliver oxygen at 40L/min, 37°C, and 99.9% relative humidity.
• The high-flow oxygen is delivered directly to the nasopharynx. This produces FiO2 equal to that delivered by traditional mask devices.
• The benefits of HFNC include reduced work of breathing, improved gas exchange by nasopharyngeal dead-space washout, and decreased energy required to humidify and heat respiratory gases.

The HFNC equipment shown in the image below uses a heated humidifier (named PMH200), a nasal cannula (no. 2), and a ventilator (brand: vivo30).

Other options:

Option a: Mechanical ventilator

Option b: Infusion Pump

Option c: CPAP

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: On your morning walk in the park, you notice an unconscious man lying on the ground. Which of the following options would be the next best step?
options: Check carotid pulse, start CPR, and call for help; Defibrillate if no pulse.
Call for help, check pulse, do CPR, defibrillate if no pulse
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Call for help, check pulse, do CPR, defibrillate if no pulse

The next best step is to Call for help, check pulse, do CPR, defibrillate If no pulse.

Steps in basic life support:

First step – Assess safety of the surroundings.

Second step - Assess for responsiveness

Third step – Proceed if the patient is unresponsive. Shout for help.

If the patient is unresponsive, assess for breathing and carotid pulse simultaneously for no more than 10 seconds.

In the given scenario, it is already mentioned that you are in a park (scene safety has been assessed), and that the person is unconscious (responsiveness has been assessed). So, the immediate next step is to call for help, and start CPR.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: The blue pipeline in the operation theatre is used for delivering which of the following gases?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Nitrous oxide

The blue pipeline in operation theatre is for nitrous oxide.

Other options:

Oxygen: White

Air: Black

Vacuum/Central suction: Yellow

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: The given set of instruments are used in:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Airway management

The image shows a tray in an airway cart with the instruments necessary for airway management.

An airway cart may include:

• Laryngoscope blades of various sizes, including a rigid fibreoptic.
• Tracheal tubes of various sizes, and tracheal tube guides such as semirigid stylets, ventilating tube changer, light wands, and forceps that are required to manipulate the distal portion of the tracheal tube.
• Masks of various sizes.
• Laryngeal mask airways of various sizes.
• Flexible fiberoptic intubation equipment.
• Retrograde intubation equipment.
• At least one device to perform emergency noninvasive airway ventilation such as esophageal tracheal tube, a hollow jet ventilation stylet.
• Equipment required for emergency invasive airway access.
• An exhaled CO2 detector.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text:
Which of the following can be considered as effective CPR?

1. Respiratory rate: 20 - 24 breaths per minute.

2. Chest compressions: 100-120/min.

3. Allow complete chest recoil.

4. 5-6 cm depression.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 2, 3, and 4

The ideal rescue breath rate for adults is 10 breaths/min, while in infants and children up to puberty it is 20-30 breaths/min. As the person's age group is not specified in the question, assuming an adult, statement 1 is incorrect, while 2, 3, and 4 are correct.

Effective chest compression in adults:

• Provide 100-120 compressions per minute (30 compressions for every 15-18 sec).
• Place your arms, one over the other in the midline, on the lower 1/3rd of the patient's sternum, and lock your arms.
• Use both arms to press the chest to a depth of 5-6 cm (2 - 2.4 inches) or more.
• Press hard and fast
• Allow for full chest recoil after every compression.

Effective chest compressions in a child older than 1 year and up to puberty:

• The compression rate is 100 - 120/min  (30 compressions for every 15-18 sec).
• One or both palms are placed in the midline.
• The depth of compression is 2 inches.
• Press hard and fast
• Allow for full chest recoil after every compression.

Effective chest compressions in infants (<1 year):

• 100 to 120 compressions per minute (30 compressions for every 15-18 sec).
• One provider: Place two fingers, one between the nipple line and the other 1 cm below.
• Two providers: Encircle the infant's torso with both hands with both thumbs pointing cephalic positioned 1cm below the nipples over the sternum.
• Depth of compressions should be at least 1.5 inches or 1/3 the depth of the infant’s chest.
• Press hard and fast
• Allow for full chest recoil after every compression.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 32-year-old male presents with severe respiratory distress due to aspiration risk and requires rapid sequence intubation. Which is the correct procedural sequence?
options: Preoxygenation → Induction → Paralysis → Intubation → Confirmation → Post-intubation care
Induction → Preoxygenation → Paralysis → Intubation → Confirmation → Post-intubation care
Paralysis → Induction → Intubation → Post-intubation care → Confirmation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Preoxygenation → Induction → Paralysis → Intubation → Confirmation → Post-intubation care

Rapid sequence intubation (RSI) follows a strict, time-critical sequence to minimize aspiration and hypoxia. Preoxygenation maximizes oxygen reserves. Induction with a sedative ensures unconsciousness, followed immediately by paralysis to facilitate optimal intubating conditions. This is followed by intubation, confirmation of tube placement (end-tidal CO₂, chest rise, auscultation), and post-intubation care including ventilation, sedation, and securing the tube.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 40-year-old man develops sudden choking while eating a large piece of food. He becomes severely distressed, and attempts at endotracheal intubation in the hospital are unsuccessful. What is the most appropriate next step to secure the airway?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Cricothyroidotomy

Cricothyroidotomy is the emergency surgical airway of choice in a “can’t intubate, can’t oxygenate” (CICO) situation. It provides the fastest access to the airway through the cricothyroid membrane and is lifesaving in patients with acute upper airway obstruction when endotracheal intubation has failed.

Why not the other options?

• A. Repeat endotracheal intubation: Repeated attempts delay oxygenation and increase the risk of hypoxia in a failed airway.
• B. Laryngeal mask airway (LMA): May be useful as a rescue supraglottic airway but is not reliable in complete upper airway obstruction caused by an impacted foreign body.
• C. Tracheostomy: Provides a definitive airway but is more time-consuming and is not the preferred emergency procedure in a CICO scenario.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 40-year-old man is administered succinylcholine to facilitate rapid sequence intubation. During intraoperative neuromuscular monitoring, a 50-Hz tetanic stimulus is applied. The anesthesiologist observes a sustained muscle contraction without any fade throughout the tetanic stimulation. This finding is most characteristic of which type of neuromuscular blockade?
options: Both non-depolarizing and Phase-II depolarizing blockade
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Phase-I depolarizing neuromuscular blockade

A Phase-I depolarizing block, typically produced by standard doses of succinylcholine, results from persistent depolarization of the motor end plate. Since succinylcholine acts as a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist, neuromuscular transmission remains uniformly depressed without presynaptic receptor blockade.

Consequently:

• Tetanic stimulation shows a sustained response without fade.
• Train-of-four (TOF) stimulation shows equal reduction in all twitches.
• Post-tetanic facilitation is absent.
• Anticholinesterases prolong or enhance the block.

In contrast, Phase-II depolarizing block and non-depolarizing blockade both exhibit tetanic fade, TOF fade, and post-tetanic facilitation because they impair normal neuromuscular transmission in a manner similar to competitive blockade.

Other Options:

• Option A. Non-depolarizing neuromuscular blockade: Incorrect. Competitive neuromuscular blockers produce tetanic fade due to presynaptic inhibition of acetylcholine release.
• Option C. Phase-II depolarizing neuromuscular blockade: Incorrect. With prolonged or repeated succinylcholine exposure, the block resembles a non-depolarizing block and demonstrates tetanic fade.
• Option D. Both non-depolarizing and Phase-II depolarizing blockade: Incorrect. Both exhibit fade, not a sustained tetanic response.

Educational Objective:

• A sustained response to tetanic stimulation without fade is the hallmark of Phase-I depolarizing neuromuscular blockade caused by standard-dose succinylcholine.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 45-year-old woman is undergoing posterior fossa surgery for excision of a cerebellopontine angle tumor. During the procedure, the neurophysiology team uses intraoperative evoked potential monitoring to assess brainstem integrity. The anesthesiologist selects the modality that is least affected by general anesthetic agents to ensure reliable monitoring throughout surgery. Which of the following is most resistant to the effects of anesthesia?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Brainstem Auditory Evoked Response (BAER)

• Brainstem Auditory Evoked Response (BAER) is the least affected by anesthetic agents among commonly monitored evoked potentials.
• Although most anesthetics reduce the amplitude and prolong the latency of evoked responses, BAER remains relatively stable, making it the preferred modality for monitoring brainstem and auditory pathway function during posterior fossa and cerebellopontine angle surgeries.

Other Options:

• Option B. Visual Evoked Response (VER): Incorrect. VER is highly sensitive to volatile and intravenous anesthetics, making intraoperative recordings less reliable.
• Option C. Somatosensory Evoked Potential (SSEP): Incorrect. SSEPs are moderately suppressed by anesthetic agents, particularly volatile anesthetics, which decrease amplitude and prolong latency.
• Option D. Electroencephalogram (EEG): Incorrect. EEG records spontaneous cortical electrical activity, not evoked responses, and is highly influenced by anesthetic depth.

Educational Objective:

Among intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring techniques, BAER is the most resistant to anesthetic-induced changes, making it the preferred modality for assessing brainstem function during neurosurgical procedures involving the posterior fossa and auditory pathways.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 48-year-old man is undergoing prolonged abdominal surgery under total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA). The anesthesiologist wants to minimize the risk of intraoperative awareness while avoiding excessive anesthetic depth. A monitor is used to continuously assess the patient's level of consciousness by analyzing electroencephalographic (EEG) activity. Which of the following monitoring modalities is most appropriate for this purpose?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Bispectral Index (BIS) monitoring

Bispectral Index (BIS) monitoring is an EEG-based technique that provides an objective assessment of the depth of anesthesia. It generates a numerical score ranging from 0 to 100, reflecting the patient's level of consciousness.

• 0: No detectable cortical electrical activity
• 40–60: Optimal depth for general anesthesia
• 60–100: Increasing levels of consciousness with a higher risk of awareness

BIS monitoring is particularly useful during total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA), where there is no end-tidal anesthetic concentration to estimate anesthetic depth.

Other Options:

• Option A. Pulse oximetry: Incorrect. Pulse oximetry monitors arterial oxygen saturation and pulse rate but provides no information about the depth of anesthesia or patient awareness.
• Option B. Colour Doppler ultrasonography: Incorrect. Colour Doppler evaluates blood flow within vessels and has no role in monitoring anesthetic depth.
• Option D. End-tidal CO₂ monitoring: Incorrect. Capnography assesses ventilation, airway patency, and endotracheal tube placement but does not measure consciousness or cortical activity.

Educational Objective:

Bispectral Index (BIS) monitoring is the most reliable objective method for assessing the depth of anesthesia by analyzing EEG activity. Maintaining a BIS value between 40 and 60 helps reduce the risk of intraoperative awareness while avoiding unnecessarily deep anesthesia.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 54-year-old woman is undergoing laparoscopic hysterectomy under general anesthesia. BIS monitoring is applied. The BIS value reads 85 during trocar insertion. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Patient has regained consciousness/light anesthesia

BIS (Bispectral Index) estimates depth of hypnosis. Typical targets for general anesthesia are \~40–60. A BIS of 85 indicates light anesthesia/near-awake state, with high risk of awareness and inadequate hypnotic depth during a noxious stimulus like trocar insertion. The anesthetic should be deepened (increase volatile/propofol, ensure analgesia) while assessing clinical signs and artifacts.

| BIS Values | Condition

| ---------- | ---------

| 100 | Awake

| 65–85 | Sedation

| 45–65 | General anaesthesia

| < 40 | Burst suppression

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 62-year-old obese male with OSA is scheduled for awake fiberoptic intubation. To increase apneic time and improve oxygenation during induction, the anesthesiologist applies THRIVE. Which mechanism best explains its benefit?
options: Generates positive end-expiratory pressure and apneic oxygenation
Increases FiO₂ but reduces CO₂ clearance
Increases minute ventilation without airway instrumentation
Allows spontaneous ventilation through bypass circuits
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Generates positive end-expiratory pressure and apneic oxygenation

THRIVE = High-flow nasal oxygen during apnea

Benefits:

• extends safe apnea time
• provides low-level PEEP
• humidified + warmed gas
• useful in obese + OSA + difficult airway

CO₂: not fully eliminated, accumulates but slower

THRIVE = Transnasal Humidified Rapid Insufflation Ventilatory Exchange

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A child presents with acute respiratory distress. On examination, the abdomen was scaphoid. Which of the following should not be performed in this patient:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Bag and mask ventilation

A scaphoid abdomen with respiratory distress suggests congenital diaphragmatic hernia, where bag–mask ventilation can worsen gastric insufflation and further compromise lung expansion. Oxygen and intubation with gentle PPV are appropriate; bag–mask ventilation must be avoided.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A child was being delivered oxygen by nasal canula at 3L/min. What is the FiO2 being delivered?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 30%

FiO₂ increases by about 4% per litre of oxygen flow.

Starting from room air (21%): Nasal cannula delivers FiO₂ ≈ 21% + 4% per L/min.

At 3 L/min → 21% + (3 × 4%) = 32%, but standard clinical rounding places it closest to 30% for exam purposes.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A conscious patient with trismus requires maintenance of airway patency. Which airway adjunct is most appropriate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Nasopharyngeal airway

A nasopharyngeal airway (NPA) bypasses the gag reflex and can safely be used in conscious or lightly sedated patients, particularly when mouth opening is limited.

Educational Objective:

An NPA is useful in patients with an intact gag reflex, trismus, limited mouth opening, or cervical spine injury.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A newly renovated operating theatre is having essential anesthesia equipment installed. During routine inspection of the anesthesia workstation, the technician suddenly develops lightheadedness and nausea. He immediately switches off the anesthesia machine and leaves the room. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Leakage of Nitrous Oxide

Nitrous oxide exposure causes:

• dizziness
• nausea
• euphoria / disorientation
• headache
• diffusion hypoxia (with sudden discontinuation)

It is also the most common anesthetic gas associated with chronic occupational exposure issues, especially in poorly scavenged OTs.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A patient diagnosed with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) has a PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio below 100, consistent with severe ARDS. What should be the next appropriate ventilatory management strategy for this patient?
options: Low PEEP and high tidal volume
High PEEP and low tidal volume
High tidal volume with prolonged expiratory pause
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. High PEEP and low tidal volume

Severe ARDS (PaO₂/FiO₂ < 100) requires lung-protective ventilation, which includes low tidal volume (≈6 mL/kg PBW) to prevent volutrauma, barotrauma and high PEEP to maintain alveolar recruitment and improve oxygenation. Prone positioning is helpful but not the first step; the cornerstone strategy remains high PEEP + low tidal volume.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A patient is expected to require mechanical ventilation for several days in the intensive care unit. To minimize the risk of tracheal mucosal injury, the anesthesiologist selects an endotracheal tube with the most appropriate cuff design. Which type of cuff is preferred?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. High-volume, low-pressure cuff

Modern endotracheal tubes are equipped with high-volume, low-pressure cuffs, which distribute pressure over a larger contact area, reducing mucosal ischemia and tracheal injury while providing an effective airway seal.

Educational Objective:

High-volume, low-pressure cuffs are preferred because they reduce tracheal mucosal damage while maintaining an adequate seal for positive-pressure ventilation.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A patient is intubated with a high-volume, low-pressure cuffed endotracheal tube for a prolonged surgical procedure. The anesthesiologist periodically measures cuff pressure to prevent tracheal mucosal ischemia. What is the maximum recommended cuff pressure?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 25 cm H₂O

Endotracheal cuff pressure should be maintained ≤25 cm H₂O to avoid tracheal mucosal ischemia, recurrent laryngeal nerve injury, and post-intubation tracheal stenosis. The cuff should be inflated only until an adequate seal is achieved.

Educational Objective:

Maintain cuff pressure below 25 cm H₂O and monitor it periodically, especially when nitrous oxide is used, as it diffuses into the cuff and increases cuff pressure.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: According to the Difficult Airway Society (DAS) guidelines for unanticipated difficult intubation in adults, which of the following represents the correct sequence of airway interventions prioritizing oxygenation?
options: Intubation → Front of neck access → SAD → Face mask ventilation
Intubation → SAD → Face mask ventilation → Front of neck access
Face mask ventilation → Intubation attempts → SAD → Front of neck access
SAD → Intubation → Front of neck access → Face mask ventilation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Intubation → SAD → Face mask ventilation → Front of neck access

The DAS algorithm consists of four sequential plans:

• Plan A: Tracheal intubation

• Optimize first-pass success (positioning, bougie/videolaryngoscope if needed).
• Limit attempts (generally ≤3, with one additional attempt by an experienced operator).

• Plan B: Maintain oxygenation using a supraglottic airway (SGA)

• Insert a second-generation SGA.
• Consider intubation through the SGA only in appropriate circumstances.

• Plan C: Face-mask ventilation and wake the patient

• If intubation and SGA fail but mask ventilation is possible, maintain oxygenation and abandon the procedure if feasible.

• Plan D: Emergency front-of-neck access (eFONA)

• Performed in a Can't Intubate, Can't Oxygenate (CICO) situation.
• The recommended technique is scalpel-bougie cricothyroidotomy.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: AMBU AURA40 is what generation LMA?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. First

AMBU AURA40 is a first-generation LMA because it has a single airway tube, lacks a gastric drainage channel, and functions as a reusable variant of the classic LMA. The “40” denotes up to 40 uses(made of silicone and can be autoclaved up to 40 times), unlike second-generation devices such as AuraGain that include gastric access for reduced aspiration risk.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: An ICU resident is obtaining an arterial blood gas (ABG) sample from the radial artery. Which of the following practices is incorrect while collecting the sample?
options: A normal pH does not exclude an acid-base disorder.
Fill the syringe with 0.5 mL heparin before collecting blood.
Choose an alternative artery if the modified Allen test is abnormal.
The radial artery is the preferred site for ABG sampling.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Fill the syringe with 0.5 mL heparin before collecting blood.

Only a thin coating of heparin is required to prevent clotting. The syringe should be flushed with dilute heparin and the excess expelled before sampling. Excess heparin dilutes the specimen and can alter pH and blood gas measurements.

Educational Objective:

For ABG sampling, use a heparinized syringe with only residual heparin coating, not a syringe containing heparin solution.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Arrange following parts of Anesthesia machine according to increasing pressure (from low to high): 1. Vaporizer mounting devices 2. Hanger yoke assembly 3. Flow meter assembly 4. Pipelines
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1-3-4-2

•

In the anesthesia machine, components are arranged based on the pressure of gas they handle.

•

The lowest pressure is in the low-pressure system, which includes the vaporizer mounting devices and flow meter assembly, where gas pressure is close to atmospheric. Among these, vaporizers are exposed to the lowest pressure, followed by flowmeters.

•

Next is the intermediate-pressure system, which includes the pipelines (≈45–55 psi).

•

The highest pressure is in the high-pressure system, represented by the hanger yoke assembly, which directly receives cylinder pressure (up to \~2000 psi).

Why others are incorrect:

• Other sequences misplace either the pipeline or yoke relative to low-pressure components, violating standard anesthesia machine pressure classification.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: At what pressure is the pop-up valve released in bag and mask ventilation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 30-40 cm of H₂O

In bag-and-mask ventilation, the pop-off (pressure-release) valve opens at 30–40 cm H₂O to prevent barotrauma.

This protects the neonatal lungs from excessive pressure during positive-pressure ventilation.

The valve can be overridden only in special situations like severe lung stiffness.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: During a routine inspection of the operating room, an anesthesia resident is asked to identify the medical gas cylinder containing nitrous oxide. Which of the following statements regarding the nitrous oxide cylinder is correct?
options: It is stored in a black cylinder with a white shoulder
It is stored in a blue cylinder and exists predominantly in liquid form at room temperature
The cylinder pressure decreases steadily as gas is consumed
Its critical temperature is below room temperature
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. It is stored in a blue cylinder and exists predominantly in liquid form at room temperature

Nitrous oxide is stored in blue cylinders and, because its critical temperature is 36.5°C, it exists as a liquid-vapor mixture at room temperature. The cylinder pressure remains approximately 745 psig until most of the liquid has vaporized.

Educational Objective:

Nitrous oxide is stored as a liquefied compressed gas in blue cylinders due to its high critical temperature.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: During anaesthesia, a patient is encountered in a ‘cannot intubate, cannot ventilate’ (CICV) situation. What is the immediate next step in management?
options: Wake the patient up / nasal airway
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Perform needle cricothyroidotomy

A true CICV scenario represents impending hypoxic arrest. The priority is not intubation anymore, it’s oxygenation immediately. When both intubation and ventilation fail, the immediate lifesaving action is emergency front-of-neck access, most rapidly done via needle cricothyroidotomy. Attempts at further intubation or supraglottic devices waste critical time.

Option A- Give succinylcholine and retry intubation

Wrong. Paralysis may already be present and repeated attempts worsen hypoxia.

Option C- Insert supraglottic airway device

Would be correct in failed intubation if ventilation is possible.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Identify the 2nd generation supraglottic airway device from the options given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. LMA Proseal

LMA ProSeal is a second-generation supraglottic airway featuring a gastric drainage channel, improved oropharyngeal seal pressure, and enhanced protection against aspiration. The other LMAs listed are first-generation devices without gastric access.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Identify the correct size and material of MRI compatible gas cylinder.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Aluminium, Size E

MRI suites require non-ferromagnetic equipment to prevent projectile accidents and image distortion. Aluminium gas cylinders are MRI-compatible because aluminium is non-magnetic. Size E cylinders are commonly used in anesthesia and critical care as they provide an adequate oxygen supply while remaining portable and suitable for MRI environments. Hence, aluminium Size E cylinders are the standard choice for MRI-compatible gas delivery.

Why others are incorrect:

• A. Stainless steel, Size E: Ferromagnetic; unsafe in MRI.
• B. Molybdenum steel, Size A: Magnetic and contraindicated in MRI.
• D. Hard plastic, Size A: Plastic cylinders are uncommon for medical gases and Size A is impractically small for anesthesia use.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Regarding soda lime used in anesthesia breathing circuits, which of the following statements are correct except ?
options: It absorbs CO₂ by producing heat (exothermic reaction)
It can degrade sevoflurane to compound-A when dry
It turns violet when exhausted due to indicator dye
It absorbs nitrogen from the circuit during anesthesia
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. It absorbs nitrogen from the circuit during anesthesia

Soda lime absorbs carbon dioxide, not nitrogen. CO₂ reacts with water and hydroxides in soda lime, forming carbonates in an exothermic reaction, thereby removing CO₂ from the breathing circuit. Nitrogen is inert and is neither absorbed nor chemically altered by soda lime during anesthesia.

Why others are incorrect (i.e., they are true statements):

• Option A: CO₂ absorption is exothermic and produces heat.
• Option B: Dry soda lime can degrade sevoflurane to compound A.
• Option C: Exhaustion is indicated by a violet color change due to pH-sensitive dye.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: TOF ratio of 0.9 indicates:
options: Moderate blockade; not safe for extubation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Minimal blockade; safe for extubation

• Current guidelines: TOF ratio ≥0.9 → adequate recovery.
• A TOF (Train-of-Four) ratio ≥0.9 indicates adequate recovery from neuromuscular blockade with minimal residual paralysis.
• At this level, upper airway muscle tone, protective airway reflexes, and respiratory muscle strength are sufficiently restored, making it safe for extubation.
• Current anesthesia guidelines emphasize objective neuromuscular monitoring and recommend a TOF ratio of at least 0.9 to reduce postoperative residual curarization and related complications such as hypoventilation or airway obstruction.

Why others are incorrect:

• Option B: Moderate blockade corresponds to TOF ratios well below 0.9.
• Option C: Deep blockade shows absent or very weak TOF responses.
• Option D: “No blockade” implies complete recovery, but TOF 0.9 still allows minimal residual effect.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: What is considered the gold standard technique for confirmation of the correct placement of an endotracheal tube (ETT)?
options: Chest auscultation over bilateral lung fields
Fiberoptic bronchoscopy visualization of the tube in the trachea
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Fiberoptic bronchoscopy visualization of the tube in the trachea

Fiberoptic bronchoscopy is the true gold standard because it allows direct visual confirmation of the endotracheal tube passing through the vocal cords and lying within the trachea. It is definitive and independent of pulmonary blood flow or ventilation, making it especially valuable in low-flow states.

Fiberoptic bronchoscopy is the gold standard because it allows direct visualization of:

• tracheal rings
• carina
• depth & position of the tube

Why others are incorrect:

• Option A: Capnography is the clinical gold standard, but false negatives can occur in cardiac arrest or low perfusion.
• Option B: Auscultation is subjective and unreliable due to transmitted sounds.
• Option C: Chest rise can occur with esophageal or gastric ventilation and is not definitive.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: What is the composition of Amsorb?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Ca(OH)2, CaCl2, CaSO4

Amsorb is a modern CO₂ absorbent composed mainly of calcium hydroxide, with calcium chloride and calcium sulfate added to improve moisture retention and hardness. Importantly, it does not contain strong alkalis like sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide. This makes Amsorb safer because it does not degrade volatile anesthetics such as sevoflurane or desflurane into toxic byproducts (e.g., compound A or carbon monoxide), even when dry.

Why others are incorrect:

• Ca(OH)₂ + NaOH + KOH: Composition of traditional soda lime, not Amsorb.
• Ca(OH)₂ + NaOH + CaCl₂: Still contains NaOH, absent in Amsorb.
• Ba(OH)₂ + CaSO₄: Describes Baralyme, not Amsorb.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: What is the size of the endotracheal tube and blade to be used for resuscitation of a preterm neonate with weight 1.8 kg not responding to PPV?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Size 0 blade, 3 mm tube

For neonatal resuscitation, endotracheal tube size is chosen based on birth weight and gestational age. In a preterm neonate weighing \~1.8 kg, the recommended ETT size is 3.0 mm (uncuffed).

A size 0 laryngoscope blade is appropriate for preterm and small neonates to provide optimal visualization of the glottis.

Intubation is indicated when the baby does not respond to effective PPV.

Why others are incorrect:

Option B- Size 1 blade, 2.5 mm tube: Blade too large; tube usually for <1 kg neonates.

Option C- Size 0 blade, 2 mm tube: Tube too small, increases resistance and inadequate ventilation.

Option D- Size 1 blade, 1.5 mm tube: Both blade and tube sizes are inappropriate for this weight.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which among the following is the pathological basis behind refeeding syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hypophosphatemia

Refeeding syndrome is a potentially life-threatening metabolic complication that occurs when nutrition is rapidly reintroduced after prolonged starvation or severe malnutrition. The resulting insulin surge drives phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells, with hypophosphatemia being the hallmark and primary pathological abnormality.

• Hypophosphatemia is the cardinal biochemical feature of refeeding syndrome.
• Phosphate is rapidly utilized for ATP, 2,3-BPG, and phosphorylated intermediates during renewed carbohydrate metabolism, leading to profound depletion.

Why not the other options?

• A. Hypokalemia: Commonly occurs due to intracellular shift but is secondary, not the defining abnormality.
• B. Hypocalcemia: May occur occasionally but is not the characteristic feature.
• C. Hyponatremia: Can develop due to fluid retention but is not the pathological basis of refeeding syndrome.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the ideal position of a supraglottic airway device (SAB)?
options: The tip lies in the vallecula pushing the epiglottis downward
The tip lies inside the laryngeal inlet causing partial obstruction
The tip lies lateral to the glottis in the piriform fossa
The tip lies in front of the esophagus with the aperture aligned over the glottic opening
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. The tip lies in front of the esophagus with the aperture aligned over the glottic opening

An ideally positioned supraglottic airway device (SAD) sits with its distal tip resting against the upper esophageal sphincter, effectively sealing the esophagus, while the ventilatory aperture aligns directly over the glottic opening. This positioning allows unobstructed airflow into the trachea, minimizes gastric insufflation, and ensures effective ventilation without entering the larynx.

Why others are incorrect:

• Option A: Vallecular placement describes some intubating airways, not standard SAD position.
• Option B: Entry into the laryngeal inlet would obstruct airflow and cause trauma.
• Option C: Piriform fossa placement indicates malposition with poor ventilation.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which of the following cylinders can be used in patients with acute exacerbation of bronchial asthma along with oxygen?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Brown

In acute exacerbation of bronchial asthma, Heliox (helium–oxygen mixture) can be used along with oxygen to reduce airway resistance.

Helium is a low-density gas, which improves laminar flow, decreases work of breathing, and enhances aerosol drug delivery in severe airway obstruction.

Helium cylinders are color-coded brown, hence the correct choice.

Why others are incorrect:

Option A (Violet): Used for medical air or special gas mixtures, not heliox.

Option B (Blue): Represents nitrous oxide, which is contraindicated in asthma.

Option D (Orange): Used for specific industrial gases, not for respiratory therapy.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which of the following features distinguishes second-generation supraglottic airway devices from first-generation devices?
options: Presence of an inflatable cuff only
Gastric drainage channel to reduce aspiration risk
Ability to be reused multiple times
Metallic reinforcement of the airway tube
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Gastric drainage channel to reduce aspiration risk

Second-generation supraglottic airway devices incorporate a gastric access (drain) channel, improving protection against regurgitation and aspiration while providing a better airway seal.

Educational Objective:

Examples of second-generation SGAs include LMA ProSeal, i-gel, and Ambu AuraGain.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the BURP maneuver is correct?
options: It is used for preoperative airway assessment
It is a form of internal laryngeal manipulation
It is useful only during rapid-sequence induction
It is useful in difficult airways
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. It is useful in difficult airways

• The BURP maneuver (Backward, Upward, Rightward Pressure) is an external laryngeal manipulation applied to the thyroid cartilage to improve visualization of the glottis during direct laryngoscopy.
• It is commonly used when intubation is difficult (Cormack–Lehane grade II–III view) and helps improve the laryngeal view.

Why the other options are incorrect?

A. It is used for airway assessment. ❌

• Airway assessment is performed using tools such as the Mallampati classification, thyromental distance, and mouth opening.
• BURP is a laryngoscopic maneuver, not an assessment tool.

B. It is a form of internal laryngeal manipulation. ❌

• BURP is external laryngeal manipulation.
• Internal manipulation is not performed during routine intubation.

C. Useful for rapid-sequence induction. ❌

• BURP is not specific to RSI.
• It is performed whenever glottic visualization is inadequate.
• (It should not be confused with cricoid pressure (Sellick maneuver), which was historically used during RSI.)

NEET PG Pearls

| BURP Maneuver | Sellick Maneuver

| ------------- | ----------------

| Pressure on thyroid cartilage | Pressure on cricoid cartilage

| Improves glottic view | Historically used to reduce gastric aspiration during RSI

| External laryngeal manipulation | Cricoid compression

| Used in difficult intubation | Not intended to improve laryngoscopic view

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: 25-year-old make patient was given cisatracurium for neuromuscular blockade. Which of the following is not true regarding the class to which the drug belongs?
options: Their action is potentiated by Mg2+ and antagonized by Ca2+
Characteristic train of four fade present
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Metabolized by pseudo cholinesterase

•

Cisatracurium belongs to non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agents. These drugs act as competitive antagonists at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, producing paralysis. Their effect is potentiated by magnesium (reduces ACh release) and antagonized by calcium. They characteristically show train-of-four (TOF) fade due to presynaptic inhibition of acetylcholine release.

•

However, cisatracurium is not metabolized by pseudocholinesterase; it undergoes Hofmann elimination, an organ-independent process, making it safe in renal and hepatic failure.

Why others are correct:

• Competitive ACh antagonism – true
• Mg²⁺ potentiation/Ca²⁺ antagonism – true
• TOF fade – true

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 14-year-old boy with severe traumatic brain injury has been receiving a high-dose propofol infusion for sedation in the intensive care unit for the past 72 hours. He develops progressive metabolic acidosis, elevated creatine kinase levels, ventricular arrhythmias, and cardiovascular instability. The intensivist suspects Propofol Infusion Syndrome (PRIS). Which of the following findings is least likely to be associated with this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hypokalemia

Propofol Infusion Syndrome (PRIS) is a rare but potentially fatal complication associated with prolonged (>48 hours) or high-dose (>4 mg/kg/hour) propofol infusion. It is believed to result from mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired fatty acid oxidation, leading to failure of cellular energy production.

Typical features include:

• Severe metabolic (lactic) acidosis
• Rhabdomyolysis
• Hyperkalemia
• Acute cardiac dysfunction (bradyarrhythmias, cardiomyopathy, cardiovascular collapse)
• Acute kidney injury and elevated liver enzymes may also occur.

Therefore, hypokalemia is not a feature of PRIS.

Other Options:

• Option A. Metabolic acidosis: Correct. Lactic acidosis is a hallmark manifestation resulting from impaired mitochondrial oxidative metabolism.
• Option B. Rhabdomyolysis: Correct. Skeletal muscle breakdown is common and contributes to elevated creatine kinase levels, renal injury, and hyperkalemia.
• Option C. Cardiac dysfunction: Correct. PRIS can cause severe myocardial depression, arrhythmias, and refractory cardiovascular collapse, accounting for its high mortality.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 24-year-old man with multiple traumatic injuries is brought to the emergency department in hypovolemic shock. The anesthesiologist chooses ketamine for induction of anesthesia because it provides analgesia while maintaining cardiovascular stability. Its anesthetic effect is primarily mediated through blockade of which receptor?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor

• Ketamine is a dissociative anesthetic that acts primarily as a non-competitive antagonist of the NMDA receptor, a subtype of glutamate receptor in the central nervous system. By blocking NMDA receptors, ketamine inhibits excitatory neurotransmission, producing dissociative anesthesia, profound analgesia, and amnesia.
• Unlike most intravenous anesthetic agents, ketamine preserves airway reflexes, maintains spontaneous respiration, and stimulates the sympathetic nervous system, making it particularly useful in trauma, hypovolemia, and hemodynamically unstable patients.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 24-year-old young truck driver has developed a fissure in ano. What would be the ideal anesthesia for this case?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Saddle anesthesia

For fissure in ano, surgery is confined to the perineal and anal region (S2–S5 dermatomes).

Saddle anesthesia, a low-dose spinal block targeting sacral nerve roots, provides dense sensory analgesia to the perineum with minimal motor block and limited sympathetic blockade.

This allows rapid recovery, early ambulation, and is ideal for short anorectal procedures in young patients.

Why others are incorrect:

Caudal anesthesia: More commonly used in pediatrics; less predictable in adults.

Epidural anesthesia: Excessive for a minor perineal procedure.

Spinal anesthesia: Produces higher block and more hypotension than required.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 25 year old male patient was given cisatracurium for neuromuscular blockade. Which of the following is not true regarding the class to which the drug belongs?
options: Their action is potentiated by Mg2+ and antagonized by Ca2+
Characteristic train of four fade present
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Metabolized by pseudo cholinesterase

Cisatracurium is a non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocker (NDNMB) belonging to the benzylisoquinolinium group.

• Act as competitive antagonists at nicotinic (Nm) acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction
• Prevent depolarization → flaccid paralysis
• Potentiation and antagonism:

• Mg²⁺ → potentiates blockade (↓ ACh release)
• Ca²⁺ → antagonizes blockade (↑ ACh release)

• Neuromuscular monitoring:

• Shows train-of-four (TOF) fade, a hallmark of non-depolarizing block

Unique Feature of Cisatracurium:

• Undergoes Hofmann elimination (organ-independent degradation)
• Also minor ester hydrolysis
• NOT metabolized by pseudocholinesterase

Hence, option C is incorrect

Why not other options:

A. Competitive inhibition at ACh receptors: True

B. Mg²⁺ potentiation, Ca²⁺ antagonism: True

D. TOF fade present: True (characteristic of non-depolarizing block)

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 26-year-old man with no significant past history undergoes emergency appendicectomy. Rapid sequence induction is performed with thiopentone and succinylcholine 1.5 mg/kg; no other neuromuscular blocking agent is used. Surgery is completed in 35 minutes. Ninety minutes after induction, he remains apnoeic with no spontaneous respiratory effort, pupils are normal, and the train-of-four shows no response. Temperature, EtCO₂ and haemodynamics have remained normal throughout. The most appropriate management is:
options: Reverse the block with neostigmine and glycopyrrolate
Ventilate mechanically; the expected duration is 20 minutes, reflecting reduced enzyme levels
Ventilate mechanically and give fresh frozen plasma; the expected duration is 6–8 hours
Administer dantrolene, as this is an early manifestation of malignant hyperthermia
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Ventilate mechanically and give fresh frozen plasma; the expected duration is 6–8 hours

Prolonged action of succinylcholine

| Cause | Features | Duration

| ----- | -------- | --------

| ↓ Levels of pseudocholinesterase | Liver disease (acute/chronic failure); neonates, old age, pregnancy; drugs — neostigmine, pyridostigmine, anti-cancer agents | 20 min

| Atypical pseudocholinesterase (Scoline apnoea) | ↓ Metabolism of SCh; genetically determined; Ix: dibucaine number; Rx: continue mechanical ventilation + FFP | 6–8 hr

| Phase II block (resembles NDMR → fade) | Large dose ≥ 5 mg/kg → receptor damage; Rx: ventilate, await spontaneous recovery, do NOT use neostigmine | —

Dibucaine number

| Point | Detail

| ----- | ------

| Nature of test | Qualitative analysis of enzyme activity (not quantitative)

| Principle | Dibucaine (a local anaesthetic) binds normal pseudocholinesterase and inhibits it

| Normal | \~80

| Homozygous atypical variant | \~20

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 26-year-old pregnant woman receives epidural anesthesia. Immediately following the injection of lidocaine with epinephrine through the epidural catheter, the patient complains of perioral numbness and becomes very apprehensive. Her heart rate is 110/min and her BP is 90/60 mmHg. What is this most likely due to?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Accidental intravascular injection

• Perioral numbness and apprehension occurring immediately after epidural injection of lidocaine with epinephrine strongly suggest intravascular injection.
• Early CNS symptoms (perioral numbness, anxiety) reflect local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST), while tachycardia indicates intravascular epinephrine. Hypotension may follow due to systemic vasodilation or evolving toxicity.
• This is why an epinephrine-containing test dose is used—to unmask intravascular placement promptly.

Why others are incorrect:

• A. Accidental subdural injection: Causes delayed, patchy, high sensory block—not immediate CNS signs.
• B. Accidental subarachnoid injection: Produces rapid dense spinal block with severe hypotension/bradycardia.
• D. Allergy to lignocaine: Rare; presents with rash, bronchospasm, or anaphylaxis, not perioral numbness.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 28-year-old man with multiple traumatic injuries is brought to the emergency department in hemorrhagic shock. General anesthesia is planned for emergency laparotomy. Ketamine is selected as the induction agent because it helps maintain cardiovascular stability. Which property of ketamine is primarily responsible for this effect?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Indirect sympathomimetic activity

Ketamine inhibits the neuronal reuptake of catecholamines, resulting in increased sympathetic activity. This indirect sympathomimetic effect raises heart rate, blood pressure, and cardiac output, making ketamine particularly useful in patients with hypovolemia or hemorrhagic shock.

Educational Objective:

Ketamine is the IV induction agent of choice in hemorrhagic shock because its indirect sympathomimetic action maintains cardiovascular function despite its mild direct myocardial depressant effect.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 28-year-old woman undergoes an elective lower segment Caesarean section. As part of her postoperative pain management, the anesthesiologist performs an ultrasound-guided Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block. Which of the following statements regarding the TAP block are incorrect? 1. The Triangle of Petit is the landmark used in the landmark-guided technique. 2. It can be used as the sole anesthetic for an open appendectomy. 3. It is an effective technique for postoperative analgesia after Caesarean section. 4. It blocks the thoracic nerves from T4 to T8.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2 and 4

• The Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block is a regional anesthesia technique in which local anesthetic is injected into the fascial plane between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles. It blocks the anterior rami of T6–L1 nerves (most consistently T10–L1) supplying the anterolateral abdominal wall, providing somatic postoperative analgesia.
• It is not suitable as the sole anesthetic for procedures such as appendectomy because it does not provide visceral analgesia. Instead, it is widely used as part of a multimodal analgesic regimen after abdominal surgeries, particularly Caesarean section, hernia repair, and abdominal wall procedures.

Other Options:

• Statement 1. The Triangle of Petit is the landmark used in the landmark-guided technique: Correct. The Triangle of Petit is the classical landmark for the landmark-guided TAP block, although ultrasound guidance is now preferred.
• Statement 3. It is an effective technique for postoperative analgesia after Caesarean section: Correct. TAP block is commonly used for postoperative analgesia following Caesarean section, especially when neuraxial opioids are not used or are contraindicated.

Educational Objective:

• A TAP block provides somatic analgesia of the anterior abdominal wall (approximately T6–L1) and is primarily used for postoperative pain relief after abdominal surgery.
• It does not provide visceral anesthesia and therefore cannot serve as the sole anesthetic for intra-abdominal procedures such as appendectomy.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 30-year-old woman is scheduled for laparoscopic sterilization as a day-care procedure. The anesthesiologist chooses a neuromuscular blocking agent that has a rapid onset, intermediate duration, and can be rapidly reversed with sugammadex, allowing early discharge. Which of the following is the preferred muscle relaxant?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Rocuronium

Rocuronium is an intermediate-acting non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocker with rapid onset. Its effects can be rapidly and completely reversed using sugammadex, making it ideal for ambulatory (day-care) surgery.

Educational Objective:

For day-care surgery, rocuronium is the preferred neuromuscular blocker because it combines rapid onset, predictable recovery, and rapid reversal with sugammadex.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 30-year-old woman is undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. Shortly after intravenous administration of a neuromuscular blocking agent before induction is complete, she complains of severe burning pain at the injection site and withdraws her arm. Which of the following neuromuscular blocking agents is most commonly associated with marked pain on intravenous injection?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Rocuronium

• Rocuronium is the non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocker most frequently associated with pain on intravenous injection.
• The pain is typically immediate, burning, or stinging and is thought to result from its low pH and direct irritation of the vascular endothelium. Without preventive measures, injection pain occurs in 50–80% of patients.
• To reduce discomfort, intravenous lidocaine pretreatment or administration after induction with propofol is commonly employed.

Other Options:

• Option A. Succinylcholine: Incorrect. Succinylcholine is more commonly associated with postoperative myalgia rather than significant pain on injection.
• Option B. Vecuronium: Incorrect. Vecuronium causes minimal or no injection pain because of its relatively neutral formulation.
• Option D. Cisatracurium: Incorrect. Cisatracurium is generally well tolerated on injection and rarely causes significant discomfort.

Educational Objective:

• Among commonly used neuromuscular blocking agents, rocuronium is the most likely to cause severe pain on intravenous injection.
• Pretreatment with lidocaine or administering the drug after induction of anesthesia significantly reduces this adverse effect.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 32-year-old man undergoes elective surgery under general anesthesia. Following intravenous administration of succinylcholine (1 mg/kg) for endotracheal intubation, he develops prolonged apnea requiring continued mechanical ventilation. Laboratory evaluation reveals a normal serum pseudocholinesterase concentration, but the dibucaine number is 50. What is the most likely duration of neuromuscular paralysis in this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Paralysis lasting 20–30 minutes

A dibucaine number of approximately 50 indicates a heterozygous atypical pseudocholinesterase variant. Although the amount of pseudocholinesterase is normal, the enzyme has reduced ability to hydrolyze succinylcholine, leading to an intermediate prolongation of neuromuscular blockade.

• Normal dibucaine number (\~80): Paralysis lasts about 5–10 minutes (approximately 9–14 minutes).
• Heterozygous atypical enzyme (dibucaine number \~50): Paralysis is prolonged to 20–30 minutes.
• Homozygous atypical enzyme (dibucaine number \~20): Paralysis may persist for 1–3 hours or longer.

Other Options:

• Option A. Hyperkalemic cardiac arrest: Although succinylcholine can precipitate life-threatening hyperkalemia in patients with burns, denervation injuries, or neuromuscular disorders, this complication is unrelated to the dibucaine number.
• Option B. Paralysis lasting 5–10 minutes: This is the expected duration in individuals with normal pseudocholinesterase function and a dibucaine number of about 80.
• Option D. Paralysis lasting more than 1–3 hours: Such marked prolongation is characteristic of homozygous atypical pseudocholinesterase deficiency (dibucaine number around 20), not a dibucaine number of 50.

Educational Objective:

• The dibucaine number reflects the quality (functional activity) of pseudocholinesterase rather than its quantity.
• A dibucaine number of 50 is consistent with heterozygous atypical pseudocholinesterase, resulting in intermediate prolongation of succinylcholine-induced paralysis (20–30 minutes).

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 35-year-old man is undergoing induction of general anesthesia. The anesthesiologist wishes to select an intravenous induction agent that is least likely to cause pain during injection. Which of the following agents is least commonly associated with injection pain?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Ketamine

Unlike propofol, etomidate, and concentrated thiopentone solutions, ketamine does not typically cause pain on intravenous injection. In fact, because of its intrinsic analgesic properties, it is generally well tolerated during administration.

Educational Objective:

Ketamine is the IV induction agent least likely to produce injection pain, whereas propofol is the most commonly implicated.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 35-year-old man with a traumatic brain injury is posted for emergency craniotomy. He has clinical and radiological evidence of raised intracranial pressure (ICP). While planning anesthesia, the anesthesiologist avoids an agent that may increase cerebral blood flow and further elevate ICP. Which of the following anesthetic agents is most likely to increase intracranial pressure?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Sevoflurane

• Sevoflurane is a volatile inhalational anesthetic that causes cerebral vasodilation, resulting in increased cerebral blood flow (CBF). This increase in CBF can lead to a rise in intracranial pressure (ICP), particularly at higher concentrations or in patients with impaired intracranial compliance.
• In contrast, most intravenous induction agents reduce cerebral metabolic activity, leading to a secondary reduction in cerebral blood flow and ICP.

Effect of Common Anesthetic Agents on ICP

| Anesthetic Agent | Effect on ICP | Mechanism

| ---------------- | ------------- | ---------

| Sevoflurane | ↑ Increases | Cerebral vasodilation → ↑ CBF

| Thiopentone sodium | ↓ Decreases | Reduces cerebral metabolic rate and CBF

| Propofol | ↓ Decreases | Reduces cerebral metabolism and CBF

| Lidocaine | Neutral or slight ↓ | Blunts airway reflexes and may attenuate ICP rise during laryngoscopy

Other Options:

• Option B. Thiopentone sodium: Incorrect. Thiopentone decreases cerebral metabolic rate, cerebral blood flow, and ICP, making it useful in neuroanesthesia.
• Option C. Lidocaine: Incorrect. Intravenous lidocaine has little effect on baseline ICP and is often administered before laryngoscopy to attenuate transient increases in ICP.
• Option D. Propofol: Incorrect. Propofol decreases cerebral metabolic demand and cerebral blood flow, thereby lowering ICP and is widely used in patients with raised intracranial pressure.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 36-year-old man undergoes elective soft tissue surgery under local anesthesia. A long-acting local anesthetic is injected intramuscularly for postoperative analgesia. Three days later, he complains of persistent pain and tenderness at the injection site, along with difficulty contracting the affected muscle. Examination reveals localized muscle weakness without sensory deficits or systemic toxicity. Which of the following local anesthetics is most likely responsible for these findings?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Bupivacaine

The patient has local anesthetic-induced myotoxicity, characterized by skeletal muscle fiber necrosis at the site of injection.

Among commonly used local anesthetics, bupivacaine has the greatest myotoxic potential, particularly after intramuscular infiltration or continuous infusion.

Mechanism of myotoxicity

Local anesthetics can directly injure skeletal muscle by:

• Disrupting muscle cell membranes
• Increasing intracellular calcium concentration
• Causing mitochondrial dysfunction
• Leading to myonecrosis, followed by regeneration over weeks

Clinical features

• Localized muscle pain
• Tenderness
• Weakness of the injected muscle
• Elevated CK (occasionally)
• No systemic neurological or cardiovascular manifestations unless toxic plasma levels are reached

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 36-year-old man undergoes ultrasound-guided brachial plexus block for upper limb surgery. While discussing the pharmacology of local anesthetics, the anesthesiologist explains why bupivacaine produces effective nerve blockade at lower concentrations than lignocaine. Which property is the primary determinant of the potency of a local anesthetic?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Lipid solubility

• The potency of local anesthetics is primarily determined by their lipid solubility. Since peripheral nerves are surrounded by lipid-rich membranes, highly lipid-soluble drugs penetrate these membranes more efficiently and require lower concentrations to achieve effective nerve blockade.
• For example, bupivacaine is more lipid-soluble and therefore more potent than lignocaine.

Other Options:

• Option A. pKa: Incorrect. The pKa determines the onset of action. Drugs with a pKa closer to physiological pH have a larger non-ionized fraction and therefore a faster onset.
• Option B. Molecular weight: Incorrect. Molecular weight has no significant role in determining the clinical potency of local anesthetics.
• Option D. Protein binding: Incorrect. Protein binding primarily influences the duration of action. Drugs with higher protein binding remain attached to sodium channels longer, producing prolonged anesthesia.

Educational Objective:

• The pharmacological properties of local anesthetics are determined by different physicochemical characteristics:

• Potency → Lipid solubility
• Onset of action → pKa
• Duration of action → Protein binding

• Remember the classic association:

• More lipid soluble = More potent
• Lower pKa = Faster onset
• Greater protein binding = Longer duration

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 39-year-old woman is scheduled for craniotomy for excision of a frontal lobe tumor. Preoperative imaging shows raised intracranial pressure (ICP). The anesthesiologist plans to use a volatile anesthetic that minimally increases cerebral blood flow and best preserves cerebral autoregulation. Which of the following inhalational anesthetics is the preferred choice in this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Sevoflurane

Among volatile anesthetics, sevoflurane produces the least cerebral vasodilation and best preserves cerebral autoregulation, making it the preferred inhalational anesthetic for patients with raised intracranial pressure undergoing neurosurgery.

Educational Objective:

Sevoflurane is the volatile anesthetic of choice in neurosurgical patients because it causes minimal increase in cerebral blood flow and ICP compared with other inhalational agents.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 4-year-old child is brought to the emergency department in cardiac arrest. High-quality CPR is initiated, and intravenous access cannot be obtained despite repeated attempts. The resuscitation team decides to establish intraosseous (IO) access for administration of epinephrine. Which of the following is the preferred site for intraosseous cannulation in this child?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Proximal tibia

The proximal tibia is the preferred site for intraosseous access in children because it is easily accessible and provides rapid entry into the systemic circulation through the marrow venous plexus.

Educational Objective:

In pediatric emergencies where IV access cannot be established promptly, the proximal tibia is the first-choice site for intraosseous vascular access.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 4-year-old child is scheduled for elective herniotomy. An inhalational induction is planned because intravenous access has not yet been established. The anesthesiologist avoids one volatile anesthetic because of its marked airway irritability and high incidence of laryngospasm during induction. Which of the following inhalational anesthetics is not recommended for inhalational induction in children?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Desflurane

Desflurane is highly pungent and irritates the airway, frequently causing coughing, breath-holding, and laryngospasm. Consequently, it is not suitable for inhalational induction, especially in pediatric patients. Sevoflurane remains the preferred inhalational induction agent because it is non-pungent and well tolerated.

Educational Objective:

Sevoflurane is the inhalational induction agent of choice in children, whereas desflurane is avoided because of its airway irritant properties.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 4-year-old collapses. Two rescuers are present. Which is the correct compression:ventilation ratio and technique for this pre-pubertal child with 2 rescuers?
options: 15:2 with two-thumb technique at lower 1/3rd of sternum
15:2 with heel of one hand only
30:2 with one hand, compression depth 2 cm
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 15:2 with heel of one hand only

A 4-year-old is a pre-pubertal child, and during two-rescuer CPR, the recommended compression-to-ventilation ratio is 15:2. Chest compressions are delivered over the lower half of the sternum using the heel of one hand, or two hands if required depending on the child's size, to achieve a depth of at least one-third of the anteroposterior chest diameter (≈5 cm). The two-thumb encircling technique is reserved for infants (<1 year) during two-rescuer CPR, while a 30:2 ratio is used for single-rescuer CPR regardless of age.

| Age | Single Rescuer | Two Rescuers | Compression Technique

| --- | -------------- | ------------ | ---------------------

| Infant (<1 year) | 30:2 | 15:2 | Two-thumb encircling (preferred)

| Child (1 year to puberty) | 30:2 | 15:2 | Heel of one hand (or two hands if needed)

| Adult | 30:2 | 30:2 | Two hands

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: A 40-year-old female posted for Laparoscopic cholecystectomy with history of hypertension and ischemic heart disease. All of the following medications may be continued except?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Clopidogrel

For elective non-cardiac surgery, clopidogrel is usually discontinued 5–7 days before the procedure because it irreversibly inhibits platelet function and significantly increases the risk of perioperative bleeding.
